paper_sections.title: Sleep discrepancy between self-report and PSG
Exploratory correlation analysis between functional connectivity and sleep discrepancy

description.value: A simultaneous EEG-fMRI study examining anterior-insula-based functional connectivity across wakefulness and NREM sleep stages in patients with insomnia disorder and healthy controls, including associations with sleep discrepancy measured by the misperception index.

spans.text: Patients with insomnia disorder (n = 33) and healthy controls (n = 31) underwent simultaneous electroencephalography and functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) during nighttime sleep, and aINS-based connectivity was calculated across wake and NREM sleep.

value: The functional connectivity of the anterior insula in patients with insomnia disorder would be altered during the progression from wakefulness to NREM sleep.
The altered connectivity of the anterior insula would be associated with sleep discrepancy.

spans.text: We hypothesize that the functional connectivity of the aINS in patients with insomnia disorder would be altered during the progression from wakefulness to NREM sleep and that the altered connectivity of the aINS would be associated with sleep discrepancy.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional comparison of insomnia disorder patients and healthy controls, with simultaneous overnight EEG-fMRI recording across wakefulness and NREM sleep stages.

A significant interaction effect on connectivity between aINS and the putamen/thalamus was observed during wakefulness, as shown in  Fig. 3  and  Table 4 .

In healthy controls, the correlation between MI and left aINS–left putamen/thalamus connectivity was significantly positive during wakefulness, i.e., as the subjects attempted to fall asleep (r = 0.90,   p   < 0.001), but patients with insomnia disorder showed no significant correlation.

spans.text: The fMRI data were preprocessed using the FMRIB Software Library (FSL,   https://fsl.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl/fslwiki  , version 5.0.9) tools, the Analysis of Functional NeuroImages software package ( Cox, 1996 ) and MATLAB (MathWorks).

The fMRI data were preprocessed using the FMRIB Software Library (FSL,   https://fsl.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl/fslwiki  , version 5.0.9) tools, the Analysis of Functional NeuroImages software package ( Cox, 1996 ) and MATLAB (MathWorks).

The preprocessing steps included slice timing, motion correction, spatial normalization (voxel size, 2×2×2 mm ), nuisance signal regression, linear detrending, temporal filtering (0.01–0.08 Hz) and spatial smoothing with a 6 mm Gaussian kernel.

Using synchronous EEG-fMRI recording during wakefulness and sleep, this study aimed to investigate the brain functional connectivity of the aINS related to sleep discrepancy between self-report and PSG in patients with insomnia disorder.
